text.p: Tyson Foods Inc said Monday it expects "marked improvements" in its earnings for 1997 beginning in the second quarter.

It based its projections on recent estimates by the USDA and private forecasters that the 1996 feed grain and soybean crop will be "significantly larger" than late summer forecasts, Tyson Chairman and Chief Executive Leland Tollett said in a statement.
"As a result, we can expect much more moderate and stable feed prices for fiscal year 1997, with marked improvements in earnings beginning in the second quarter," Tollett said.
He added that demand for its product is strong, market conditions are stable and the company is "poised to take advantage of a business environment that continues to improve."
Tyson produces, processes and markets chicken and other poultry products.
